description:
Deep Calm Music | Santoor Instrumental | 1.5 Hours

Some evenings you don't need to be put to sleep. You just need to be given somewhere to land.

Monday has a way of arriving before the weekend has properly finished. By evening the body is somewhere between restless and exhausted — not quite able to relax on its own, not quite ready to sleep. There's no emergency. There's just this low-level hum that hasn't switched off yet.

This is 90 minutes of Santoor in Raga Bhairavi — a deeply warm and grounding evening raga in Indian classical music. Bhairavi doesn't push you anywhere. It just creates enough stillness around you that the noise gradually has nowhere left to go.

The Santoor is a hammered dulcimer — each note struck and then allowed to ring and fade. There's something about the way it naturally decays that gives the mind room to breathe between phrases.

🎵 What you'll hear:
- Santoor — bright struck tones that bloom into warm, ringing sustain
- Raga Bhairavi — emotionally grounding, komal-rich evening raga
- Slow unhurried phrases with natural space between them
- 90 minutes, no interruptions
- A very soft theta layer underneath (-20dB — barely there)

⏱ Chapters
0:00    Opening
20:00   Settling in
45:00   Deep calm
70:00   Still
85:00   Quiet close

🧠 How to use:
Put it on. You don't need to do anything with it. The point isn't to meditate or focus — it's just to stop. The music will do the rest.

⏱ Best for:
• Monday evening wind-down
• Mind that hasn't stopped since morning
• Restless-but-exhausted state
• Quiet background while you eat, stretch, or just sit
• Gentle transition toward sleep

📺 Subscribe to Raga Focus for Indian classical music for calm, anxiety relief, and sleep.
